title: Class setup, mats and space safety
audience: Yoga and Pilates instructors who set up classes in studios, halls, homes, gardens and public parks
learningOutcomes: Set up a class space that has enough room, a firm surface, clear exits and a clear path for every participant
Check mats, props and equipment before each class, and remove any item that is unsafe
State which parts of the space and permit rules are confirmed in the research and which remain open.
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Hornsby Shire Council, Commercial group fitness and personal training (no date shown); City of Stonnington, Permit for sports or personal training on public land or council facilities (no explicit date; listing metadata 13 Sep 2017).

instruction.heading: Space, room and exits
instruction.body: A class space needs room for each participant to move their arms and legs without touching another person or a wall, a clear path to the exit, and a firm floor. Check the room before each class. Look for loose boards, wet patches, cables, stored items, and furniture that could fall or be knocked. Keep the exits clear and know where they are before the class starts. Record the room, the number of participants and any hazard seen on the class record. The business's room and venue rules are held in {{business:procedures.prestart_checklist}}. Use the venue's own conditions as well as this lesson.

instruction.heading: Mats, props and equipment
instruction.body: A mat must give grip and stay flat. Check each mat for tears, lifting edges and slipperiness before the class starts, and remove any mat that is damaged. Props such as blocks, straps, bolsters and balls should be checked for cracks and for stability. Pilates equipment, such as reformers or springs, needs its own inspection under the manufacturer's instructions, and the manufacturer's manual is held as {{business:equipment.manufacturer_manual_url}}. Do not use equipment that has a loose part, a frayed strap or a spring that is not secure. Record the inspection of each item used in a class, and remove unsafe items from use with a note of the date. The approved product list for cleaning mats is in {{business:materials.approved_products}}.

instruction.heading: Heat, outdoor sessions and permits
instruction.body: Heated classes, outdoor sessions and classes in hot weather carry a risk of heat illness. Use shade, water, ventilation and breaks, and stop the class if a participant shows signs of heat distress. For outdoor classes on public land, check the council permit. Hornsby Shire Council in New South Wales names yoga and tai chi among the activities its commercial fitness permit covers (no date shown); that is council-specific. Check the permit for each park before the class.

procedure: Inspect the room for hazards, clear the path to each exit, and confirm the exits are free before the class
Check each mat for damage, grip and flatness, and remove any mat that fails
Inspect each prop and each piece of equipment, using the manufacturer's manual where one exists
Set the space so that each participant has room to move, away from walls and other participants
Check the heat, water and shade for the class, and plan breaks
Record the set-up check, the number of participants and any item removed from use

workedExamples.situation: An instructor arrives at a community hall for a morning class. One mat has a split along the middle, and the room's back door is blocked by stacked chairs.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the class start in this room?
workedExamples.reasoning: The split mat is an unsafe item and must be removed from use. The blocked exit must be cleared before the class begins, because participants need a clear route out. If the exit cannot be cleared, the class should not run in that room. The instructor should record both items and the action taken. The venue's own conditions also apply.

workedExamples.situation: A Pilates instructor plans to use a reformer in a park under a council permit. The reformer has a spring that feels loose when tested.
workedExamples.reasoning: A loose spring is an equipment fault. The reformer must be removed from use and not used in the park. The manufacturer's instructions should be checked for inspection and repair. The park permit does not make an unsafe item safe, and the record should show the fault and the removal.

equipmentAndPpe: Non-slip mats, checked before each class
Props such as blocks, straps and bolsters, checked for cracks and stability
Pilates equipment inspected under the manufacturer's instructions
Water, shade and a first-aid kit for each class
Cleaning products approved for mats, used with the label instructions

commonErrors.error: Starting a class with a blocked exit because the room looks large enough.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the exits before every class and clear any blockage before participants arrive.

commonErrors.error: Using a mat or prop with a split or loose part.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect each item before the class and remove any that fails, with a record.

commonErrors.error: Stating that a council permit covers yoga in every council.
commonErrors.prevention: Name the council and check its permit. The Hornsby position does not apply elsewhere.

commonErrors.error: Stating that a heat rule applies to every class.
commonErrors.prevention: Manage the heat risk with shade, water and breaks.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Hornsby Shire Council (NSW) names yoga and tai chi among the activities its commercial fitness permit covers. This is council-specific.
Stonnington's listing (Victoria) does not name yoga or Pilates.
Building, venue and heat rules for yoga and Pilates classes were not researched.
Completing this lesson does not grant a permit, a venue approval or any instructor licence.

qualityStandard: Every class starts with the room checked, exits clear and the set-up recorded
Every mat, prop and piece of equipment is inspected before use
Every item removed from use is recorded with the date and reason
The council permit for each public place is checked before the class
documentationEvidence: Class set-up record with the room, exits and participant count
Equipment inspection record for each item, with the date
Removed-from-use record for any unsafe item
Council permit copy for each public place used
summary: Check the room, the exits, the mats and the props before every class
Remove unsafe items from use and record each removal
Permits are council-specific; Hornsby names yoga.
Completing this lesson grants no permit, venue approval or licence

knowledgeChecks.question: A mat has a split along its middle and an exit is blocked by chairs. What is the correct action before the class?
options: Start the class, since the room is large enough for everyone in it
Ask participants to step over the split in the mat carefully today
Remove the mat from use, clear the exit, and record both items and the action

knowledgeChecks.question: Which council permit statement is accurate in this course?
options: Hornsby's commercial fitness permit names yoga; other councils' coverage is not set out in this course
Yoga is covered by every council's permit in the state and region, without any exception at all
Stonnington's permit names yoga and Pilates in its terms for the whole year ahead and the next

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a class space need, according to the lesson?
options: A soft floor for every session
Blocked exits, so participants stay close to the mats
A clear path to the exit and a firm floor
